title: 2023 budget approved; health care recruitment and strategic plan
subtitle: Also: DEI advisory committee terms, new Integrity Commissioner, surety bonds, fleet purchases, rezonings and a land sale.
overview: Council approved the 2023 budget, as amended, and later passed the budget by-law that enacts it and sets the stage for tax rates {{vote:m3}} {{vote:m18}}. Several items were deferred to staff reports or to the strategic planning process, including traffic calming, neighbourhood wellness grants, and the business licensing review. Council also approved a $10,400 increase to extend a co-op student position in the CAO's office.

Council named health care professional recruitment a priority and directed staff to work with partners on approaches the Township could take {{vote:m5}}. It approved terms of reference for a Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Advisory Committee {{vote:m12}}, appointed an Integrity Commissioner for five years {{vote:m15}}, and awarded the corporate strategic plan contract {{vote:m16}}.

Council also approved two farm rezonings, two townhouse part lot control exemptions, heritage approvals, fleet and plow truck purchases, and a surety bond policy for developers. After a closed session, Council approved selling 0.40 acres behind 151 Gregson Court for $60,000 {{vote:m24}}.

decisions.detail: Council approved the 2023 budget as amended, extended the CAO's office co-op position, and deferred several items such as traffic calming and the capital reserve increase.
Council made recruitment a priority and directed staff to work with stakeholders to propose approaches the Township could take.
Council approved the terms of reference and directed staff to start the self-nomination process.
The contract was awarded to Augustyn Enterprises Inc at an upset limit of $37,500 including disbursements, excluding HST.
John Mascarin of Aird & Berlis LLP was appointed for a five-year term starting March 1, 2023.
Council approved a revised contract with Winegard Motors and conditionally awarded two plow trucks to Premier Truck Group, pending confirmation of 2023 build spots.
Council adopted a policy accepting surety bonds as security in development agreements and directed staff to update the templates.

decisions.item: Sale of land on Gregson Court
decisions.detail: Council approved selling 0.40 acres behind 151 Gregson Court for $60,000 and authorized the CAO to sign the agreement.

debate: On health care recruitment, a delegate from the Wellington Health Care Alliance described a competitive market, a need for accommodation and office space, and rural funding rules that Groves does not qualify for. Councillors supported acting now rather than waiting for strategic planning, and one asked about a council liaison role on the working group.

On the strategic plan contract, several councillors said they could find little public information on the selected firm and wanted more on its experience and past work. Staff said bid details were confidential, that the firm had municipal strategic planning experience, and that all seven bids were near the budget.

Staff and the mayor urged Council to follow the procurement process, noting that sole-sourcing is not allowed and that sending it back could delay the plan by about a month. Councillors said they were asking the right questions and would stay involved in the process.

On the 965 Gartshore Street licence, one councillor said the Township should avoid buying prime farmland for development and urged a closer look at brownfield sites. Staff said the vacant house could be considered for housing a doctor.

On vehicle purchases, staff said the reserve can cover current costs but will be leaned on heavily, with pressure expected later in the decade. Staff said the plow trucks were urgent because of long build times.
